questions.question: Describe the main physical regions of South Africa.
questions.expected_answer: South Africa has a high interior plateau, a narrow low coastal plain around the coast and the steep Great Escarpment between them, highest in the Drakensberg. The plateau includes the high, grassy Highveld. The Lowveld is lower and hot. The Karoo is dry semi-desert, the Kalahari is dry and sandy, and Namaqualand has spring flowers.

questions.question: Explain the parts of a river system and how dams affect people.
questions.expected_answer: A river begins at its source and ends at its mouth. Tributaries join the main river to form a river system, and the land that drains into it is the catchment area. Dams store water for towns, farms and factories, make electricity and control floods, but they flood land, homes and habitats and change the river.

questions.question: Summarise how the first farmers lived.
questions.expected_answer: The first farmers settled in the summer-rainfall east about 1,800 years ago. They grew sorghum and millet with iron hoes, kept cattle, sheep and goats, and lived in homesteads of round houses around a cattle kraal. They lived alongside and integrated many Khoisan people. Chiefs governed with councils and headmen, and cattle were wealth and joined families through lobola.
